linked_issue.title: Web: restore focus after the create-incident dialog closes
linked_issue.author: Gautam-aman
linked_issue.body:
## Problem

The create-incident dialog moves keyboard focus to its first field when it opens. When a user closes it, focus does not reliably return to the control that opened the dialog. This makes keyboard navigation harder to resume.

This is separate from the open issue about adding automated accessibility checks to the whole web test suite: it fixes one concrete dialog behavior.

## Expected behavior

Opening the dialog focuses its first field. Closing with Cancel or Escape returns focus to the opener if that element is still in the document. A removed opener must not be focused.

## Where to start

- `apps/web/src/components/command/CreateIncidentDialog.tsx` — opening effect, Cancel button and Escape handler
- `apps/web/src/pages/CommandPage.tsx` — control that opens the dialog
- `apps/web/src/test/setup.ts` and `apps/web/src/App.test.tsx` — examples of the existing Vitest/Testing Library setup

One approach is to remember the active element before moving focus into the dialog, then restore it when the dialog closes. Add a focused component test; there is no need to change other modals.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Opening places focus on the first input.
- [ ] Cancel returns focus to the opener.
- [ ] Escape returns focus to the opener.
- [ ] Closing does not try to focus an opener that has been removed.
- [ ] Automated tests cover these cases.

## Testing

```bash
cd apps/web
npm run test
npm run typecheck
```

**Difficulty:** Beginner · **Estimated effort:** about 2
